$comment_rtk: Why both `git x` and `rtk git x` are allowed: RTK installs a global PreToolUse hook that rewrites `git x` into `rtk git x`, and the permission check runs on the REWRITTEN command. So the bare git patterns match nothing, and every git call a reviewer made was denied — it then fell back to reading each changed file in full, which is the expensive path and a large part of what a review pass costs. Verified directly: with only `Bash(git status:*)` allowed the call is refused; adding `Bash(rtk git status:*)` makes it run. Compaction is harmless for this use — the reviewer runs git for file lists and metadata, while the diff it actually audits arrives uncompressed in its prompt, produced by review.mjs outside the hook. There is deliberately NO `rtk dotnet test` or `rtk npm`: test output is the one thing the verdict rests on being byte-exact, and `dotnet test` is not rewritten by the hook, so denying the rtk form leaves the exact one working. Removing the rtk- entries does not restore byte-exact git output; it only returns the reviewer to being denied. See ticket #22.
$comment: Reviewer permissions. Strictly read-only. A reviewer that can edit the code it is reviewing produces a clean report that hides its own work, and its approval stops distinguishing 'this was correct' from 'this was made correct'. It may build and run tests, because verifying a claim is not the same as changing the answer. Same model as the dev agent, and that pairing is the part to preserve: a reviewer weaker than the author it audits is theatre, because it cannot catch the class of mistake the author was capable of making. Both moved from claude-opus-5 to claude-sonnet-5 on cost - a single Opus ticket run measured ~56% of a 5-hour window. Read that as a real trade and not a free win: the dev run has a human sitting on it, this one is unattended and its verdict is trusted, so a reviewer that misses a determinism bug files a clean report that hides it. If review quality visibly drops - findings that restate the diff, verdicts that miss what a human then catches - this is the FIRST knob to turn back, before the dev agent's.
